Round 2 · Implementation · Easy

Ticket #04 — Library Book Checkout

Difficulty: Easy

Context

You maintain checkout at a small library. A loan records one reader borrowing one copy. An active loan has not been returned. Readers can also reserve a book; the reservation queue gives its first reader priority over a walk-in checkout.

Practice report

Add book b1 with one copy. Check it out to reader-a as loan l1, then call return_book("l1").

Observation Current starter Expected
Return result True True
Available copies after return 0 1

To extend the case, queue reader-b and reader-c while the copy is borrowed. After the return, reader-b should be able to check out before either a walk-in or reader-c.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Available copies equal total copies minus active loans. Active loans cannot exceed the number of copies, and a successful checkout records book and reader.
  • A successful return releases exactly one copy. Unknown and repeated returns fail without changing other loans or the available-copy count.
  • Checkout honors reservation order and consumes the first reservation only when that reader checks out. A blocked checkout leaves queue order unchanged.
  • Unknown books cannot be reserved or checked out. Missing reader or loan IDs and reused loan IDs cannot create or replace a loan.

Out of Scope

Keep the supplied copy counts, in-memory storage, and reservation queue. Due dates, fines, notifications, and automatic checkout on return are outside this ticket.

Investigation

Reproduce the one-copy case and trace checkout, return, and reservation handling. Add assertions for the loan's stored state, available copies, and the next reader's checkout. Show that a repeated return cannot manufacture another copy.
